plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, low-to-moderate S still resembles the parent law, but holdout segments reaching stronger sympathetic activation reveal diminishing incremental pressure support from additional S that one shared linear-gain parent cannot match simultaneously with the low-S slope.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the saturation scale is large enough that the saturating resistance law is effectively linear over the observed S range.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes autonomic vasomotor drive recruits peripheral resistance with a constant gain across the full normalized drive range, omitting physiological saturation of vasoconstrictor effect.
plan.baseline_assumption: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite vascular smooth-muscle and arteriolar receptor recruitment causes diminishing additional peripheral resistance at high autonomic drive even while neural drive S continues to increase.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to keep the same states and feedback architecture but replace the linear S-to-resistance mapping with a saturating monotone form. The parent target relation from observed states to dP_dt is effectively governed by one shared vascular gain, so at fixed P it cannot express both a steep early vasoconstrictor effect and diminished marginal effect near high S. Varying condition: the coupled transient is observed from the prescribed initial condition while P and S evolve naturally, so different times along the trajectory sample different S levels; held fixed: posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, hormones, and the baroreflex command form. Observable contrast: under stronger hypotensive excursions that drive S toward its upper range, the child predicts flattening of the pressor benefit from further S increases, whereas the parent keeps adding resistance approximately linearly and therefore overstates late high-drive support if fitted to early low-drive behavior. This changes the scored target mapping dP_dt(P,S), not merely the auxiliary S trajectory, because the runoff denominator itself acquires different S-curvature. The effect is admissible whenever S reaches moderate to high values; if all data remain near a narrow low-S band, the refinement may be weakly identifiable, and in that restricted regime the parent is approximately recovered.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training windows with modest transients, the mechanism appears as a delayed runoff response relative to the rise or fall in S; in holdout conditions with larger or faster pressure excursions from the same initial conditions, the same lag extends into a clearer separation between early cardiac-driven and later resistance-driven pressure recovery.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the new vascular effector time constant to zero so the vascular state instantaneously equals the parent saturating function of S.
plan.promotion_reason: A finite vascular response lag cannot be represented by refitting existing static gains or the single S state, because the needed memory of past S is absent unless a separate dynamical vascular effector is introduced.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are synchronous and instantaneous once S is known, omitting the physiologic lag of vascular smooth-muscle constriction relative to neural drive.
plan.baseline_assumption: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite arteriolar smooth-muscle activation and constrictor transduction delay peripheral resistance recruitment after changes in autonomic vasomotor drive.
plan.rationale: The parent target mapping from observed states to dP_dt uses S as the sole autonomic phase variable, so once P and S are specified the resistance contribution is fixed with no memory. A realistic next refinement is to relax that single-phase assumption for the vascular branch only. Vary the magnitude and timing of the pressure displacement from the common initial conditions while holding posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormones fixed. In the parent, any early rise in S must immediately alter runoff through the same saturating resistance law, so early and late pressure recovery are locked to one shared S trajectory. This is observable for nontrivial transients where S changes appreciably and the vascular lag is comparable to the measurement window; it is weak if the lag is much shorter than all sampled times or if trajectories stay very near equilibrium. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce both the early weak-resistance response and the later stronger resistance recruitment across such conditions, because the parent has no independent temporal degree of freedom for runoff once P and S are given.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories span a moderate pressure range around and above the setpoint so that P varies enough to change cardiac ejection effectiveness, while S is still away from 0 and 1 and R is not the only changing pathway.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories, low-P recovery segments and higher-P segments can show different dP_dt sensitivity to the same S level; in holdout, the same mechanism extends this contrast to larger pressure excursions without changing background conditions.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the pressure dependence of cardiac autonomic effectiveness to zero, yielding a constant gain from S to cardiac delivery.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes autonomic drive increases cardiac delivery with one pressure-independent gain, omitting that elevated arterial pressure increases afterload and can blunt the pressure-generating benefit of sympathetic drive.
plan.baseline_assumption: Cardiac and vascular effects of autonomic drive are instantaneous relative to the modeled neural adjustment time.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Pressure-dependent cardiac afterload reduces the effective conversion of autonomic drive into arterial inflow at higher mean arterial pressure.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-gain cardiac term rather than add an unrelated process. The parent target mapping is shortcut by a single_gain assumption: at fixed R, the partial effect of S on dP_dt is constant apart from division by arterial_compliance. Scientifically, higher arterial pressure raises ventricular afterload, so the same autonomic drive need not produce the same net forward delivery into the arterial compartment at high versus low pressure. Under the stated scenario, posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormones stay fixed; the varied condition is the pressure level reached along the observed recovery trajectory, with S and P co-sampled by the solver and R retained as an existing state. The child therefore changes the target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory, by making the S-to-dP_dt slope depend on P. Observable contrast: compare segments with similar R and non-saturated S but different P; the child predicts weaker positive sensitivity of dP_dt to S at higher P than the parent can provide with one shared cardiac_delivery_gain. This is admissible for moderate pressure excursions where afterload effects are physiologically relevant and pressure remains nonnegative. Limitation: if observations remain in a very narrow pressure band or S is nearly saturated throughout, the contrast will be weak.

response_change.parent_relation: The baroreflex command for S is a fixed logistic function of P alone, so the pressure at which autonomic drive is half-activated is constant and independent of recent pressure history.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the fixed pressure half-activation with a slowly adaptive effective setpoint driven by recent pressure exposure, so the instantaneous P-to-dP_dt mapping depends on both current pressure and the history state of baroreflex resetting.
response_change.observable_effect: After a sustained pressure elevation or depression, the same instantaneous pressure P produces a different autonomic drive and therefore a different dP_dt than it does early in the trajectory; recovery weakens after prolonged exposure because the feedback threshold has shifted toward the experienced pressure.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when pressure remains displaced from the nominal setpoint for a duration comparable to or longer than a plausible baroreflex resetting time, while P traverses a range of order baroreflex_pressure_scale so that threshold motion materially changes S.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early transients still resemble the parent because resetting is initially small; in longer or more prolonged deviations, holdout trajectories show that identical current P values reached after different exposure histories produce different dP_dt, extending the same threshold-shift mechanism rather than introducing a new regime.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the resetting time constant to infinity or the resetting gain to zero, which freezes the effective setpoint at pressure_setpoint.
plan.promotion_reason: A history-dependent moving baroreflex threshold cannot be represented with the existing Markov state set {P,S,R} without conflating instantaneous neural drive with slow reflex resetting; a separate state is needed to encode recent pressure exposure.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the pressure-sensitive feedback curve is time invariant, omitting short-term baroreflex resetting/accommodation during sustained pressure perturbations.
plan.baseline_assumption: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Slow baroreceptor and central reflex resetting shifts the effective pressure setpoint toward recently experienced arterial pressure, altering autonomic responsiveness during continued non-resting conditions.
plan.rationale: The parent target mapping from observed states to dP_dt is effectively governed by a fixed baroreflex threshold: for fixed R and parameters, increasing P always suppresses S according to one unchanging logistic curve, so any two moments with the same current P and similar R are forced toward the same feedback-mediated inflow reduction. A realistic refinement is short-term baroreflex resetting, which changes that threshold after sustained pressure displacement. Under the admissible protocol, vary the duration of a pressure excursion generated from the given initial condition while holding posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormone background fixed as required. Early after the excursion begins, the child behaves close to the parent; later, the effective threshold has shifted toward the prevailing pressure, so at the same current P the child exhibits less restoring autonomic drive and therefore a different dP_dt. This is a genuine change in the scored target mapping, not only an auxiliary-state modification, because the pressure-to-dP_dt relation itself becomes history-dependent through the moving threshold. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both the early strong correction and the later weakened correction across these conditions, because changing pressure_setpoint or baroreflex_pressure_scale only selects one static logistic curve rather than a trajectory-dependent family of curves. The effect is strongest when the pressure deviation persists long enough for resetting to develop and when the deviation size is not negligible relative to baroreflex_pressure_scale; if observations are too short, the refinement may be weakly identifiable.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, asymmetric recovery is already visible in transients that traverse the effective setpoint neighborhood; in holdout, larger but still admissible deviations extend the same one-sided steepness difference, revealing curvature that a symmetric one-scale logistic cannot match with one shared parameter set.
plan.continuation_path: The child reduces to the parent in the symmetry-restoring limit where the modified pressure-command shape becomes the original logistic with one shared baroreflex_pressure_scale on both sides of the effective setpoint.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes baroreflex command has the same pressure sensitivity above and below the effective setpoint, omitting physiologically plausible asymmetry between depressor and pressor sides of the short-term reflex response.

plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's symmetric baroreflex command assumption rather than adding a new process. The parent maps effective pressure error to autonomic command through one fixed logistic threshold and scale, so after parameter refitting it still predicts mirrored pressure sensitivity around pressure_setpoint+B. Holding posture, volume status, metabolic demand, and hormones fixed as required, vary only the trajectory's pressure excursion relative to the current effective setpoint. Then compare transients that spend time moderately below versus moderately above that setpoint. In the parent, the slope of the command curve as a function of P is determined by one shared scale, so the shape of dP_dt versus P near low-pressure recovery and high-pressure suppression remains constrained to be symmetric up to the downstream inflow/runoff nonlinearities already present. In the child, the same effective pressure error produces different reflex steepness on the two sides, changing the target mapping itself because S enters the dP_dt inflow term directly and also later influences runoff through R. This is observable when the trajectory actually samples both sides of the setpoint over pressure deviations comparable to baroreflex_pressure_scale; if observations remain confined to a tiny neighborhood on one side only, the contrast may be weak and partial refitting could mimic it locally. But across both sides with one shared parameter set, the parent cannot simultaneously reproduce unequal low-pressure recovery steepness and high-pressure damping curvature if the underlying command law remains symmetric.

diagnostic_groups.name: runoff_term
diagnostic_groups.role: Peripheral runoff load opposing pressure elevation

contract.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories pass through both moderate hypotensive and hypertensive deviations relative to pressure_setpoint+B, with pressure excursions of order baroreflex_pressure_scale so the command nonlinearity is sampled on both sides rather than only infinitesimally near equilibrium.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, asymmetric recovery is already visible in transients that traverse the effective setpoint neighborhood; in holdout, larger but still admissible deviations extend the same one-sided steepness difference, revealing curvature that a symmetric one-scale logistic cannot match with one shared parameter set.
contract.continuation_path: The child reduces to the parent in the symmetry-restoring limit where the modified pressure-command shape becomes the original logistic with one shared baroreflex_pressure_scale on both sides of the effective setpoint.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Short-term arterial baroreflex signaling can show unequal gain on hypotensive versus hypertensive sides because receptor firing saturation and central efferent recruitment are not perfectly symmetric around the operating point.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective logistic slope now depends on the evolving signed pressure error, so the same parameter set produces different local curvature above and below the reset setpoint rather than a uniform rescaling.
contract.assumption_before: The pressure-sensitive feedback relation is smooth, monotone, and time invariant over the observation window, with a symmetric logistic shape around a single midpoint and one shared pressure scale.
contract.assumption_after: The baroreflex remains smooth and monotone but its pressure sensitivity varies with signed effective pressure error, producing asymmetric steepness about the reset setpoint.
contract.observable_signature: The scored target expression keeps the same algebraic dependence on S and R, but along trajectories that sample both signs of P-(pressure_setpoint+B), the successor produces unequal dP_dt-versus-P curvature on the two sides because the S command law uses a state-dependent pressure scale. This is observable for deviations on the order of baroreflex_pressure_scale with posture, blood volume, metabolic demand, and hormones held fixed.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent's single baroreflex_pressure_scale can match only one average steepness, not simultaneously the steeper hypotensive recruitment and flatter hypertensive suppression or vice versa across both sides of the effective setpoint with one shared parameter set. The change is therefore not absorbable by global coefficient retuning when both sides of the command curve are observed.

range_suggestions.baroreflex_asymmetry_gain: approximately -1 to 1; values with 1 + baroreflex_asymmetry_gain*(P - (pressure_setpoint + B))/baroreflex_pressure_scale remaining positive over the sampled trajectory preserve a monotone nonincreasing command law
